title: EU AML Regulation (AMLR) for banks | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: What the EU AMLR means for banks: CDD for accounts, transfers from EUR 1,000 and cash from EUR 3,000, linked transactions, eIDs and the EUDI Wallet.
body_markdown:
*What the EU AMLR and AMLA’s final draft standards mean for bank onboarding, occasional transactions and remote identification.*


Credit institutions are obliged entities under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies directly from 10 July 2027. A bank must apply customer due diligence when it establishes a business relationship, when it carries out an occasional transaction of EUR 10,000 or more, and when it initiates or executes an occasional transfer of funds of EUR 1,000 or more, in a single operation or through linked transactions. Under AMLA’s final draft standards, remote verification is expected to use suitable eIDs, including the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet), or relevant qualified trust services wherever possible.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Patryk Pietrzak (Head of Growth), Authologic.*
